# NOTES ON THE TEXT (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 OF 2: "Jimmy Quixote: A Novel" by Tom Gallon (Gutenberg 41754; Hurst and Blackett, London, 1906)
Dedication: to Malcolm Watson, "Your friend always, Tom Gallon, London 1906."

### BOOK I
**Ch I "Old Paul's Babies"**
- Late July. "Old Paul" (Paul Nannock) returns from London to Daisley Cross station with many parcels. Porter helps; Old Paul slings parcels with string. Forgot nothing, he thinks; forgets list when shop assistant advised on Moira's frock length. Dashes hat down, cries "Jimmy's boots!" (forgot Jimmy's boots), turns back, then realises no train possible.
- House: rambling old house (Daisley Place), low gate in old wall, path through garden.
- Patience: old servant woman, sharp, scolds, calls him "Master Paul." Children "up, not a show of bed." Supper spoilt.
- Anthony Ditchburn: older man, rusty black, peevish, forlorn, nervous hands; wants tobacco (full-flavoured). Paul brought the wrong (medium) tobacco; Ditchburn says broken packet, won't be taken back.
- Children: **Moira** (8-9, thin, dark-eyed, almost-black hair; Paul's ward; devoted to him); **Jimmy** (12-13, handsome boy; "It's been a beastly long day without you, Old Paul"); **Alice** (fair, fragile, blue eyes, "perfect child-like mouth", prim, calls on Baffalls, "Mr. Baffall saw me home").
- Shawl of many colours bought for Patience; she softens. Gifts: cricket bat and fishing rod for Jimmy; books, toys, dolls for girls; frock for Moira, two inches longer.
- Moira comes at night to Paul's room in dressing-gown: "This is the time you belong to me." Paul: "What will love do to you in the big world, Moira?"
- Backstory: Paul Nannock, tall shy blusher, rich, drifted in London; fell in love with a dark-eyed woman who loved him for three months then left for a richer man. He came to Daisley Cross, lived as hermit at Daisley Place with Patience. Later the woman (who had married and deserted for another man) sent for him on her deathbed; he brought her child **Moira**.
- **Jimmy**: parents went abroad, ship lost; guardian embezzled funds, found dead in Liverpool hovel with bullet. Paul's name was school reference.
- **Alice**: mother Mrs. Vickery (London acquaintance) left her ("Paris" excuse), never returned. Alice "Vickery".

**Ch II "And Old Paul's Friends"**
- Anthony Ditchburn arrived in storm, stayed; claims great work (monumental treatise); Paul pays for books, clothes, tobacco. Opposed Moira's staying; Paul rebukes him. Ditchburn refuses to teach children; quotes Horace; Jimmy draws in margins.
- Rev. **Temple Purdue** (small, mild, spectacled rector, widower; wife's headstone) teaches children at rectory; son **Charlie Purdue** (lonely, mischievous, Jimmy's age) joins them.
- The **Baffalls**: Daniel (Mr. Baffall, retired London businessman, grey beard fringe, twinkling grey eyes) and Mrs. Flora/"Mrs. Baffall" (childless, plump, kind, dream child). They adore the children; Mrs. Baffall: "I think I should dance, Daniel!"
- **Honora Jackman**: loud, high-voiced, single eyeglass, "fine old time," nomad, ~£150 a year; introduced by Baffalls; schemes to capture Paul for money.

**Ch III "Jimmy Quixote"**
- Honora wins Jimmy's heart; kisses him in wood. She leads him to the secret paradise (fir-cone design place, found by Paul). Paul sends her away; Jimmy calls Paul "a beast"; Paul: "Come on, Jimmy Quixote"—nicknames Jimmy "Jimmy Quixote."
- Honora's invited dinner; she sings; kisses Moira (feigned sleep).
- Honora leaves; Jimmy at station; letter signed "Honora Jackman... yours ever lovingly."

**Ch IV "The Eloping Persons"**
- Moira, jealous, asks Paul "what do you do when you love anybody?" Pair elope on donkey **the Ancient One** (bought from gipsy) in old chaise (17 shillings); breakfast at inn; return at dusk. Moira: "Promise me... never elope with anybody but me." Paul promises.
- Honora meets them at gate: "I was taking a stroll"; Paul: "We eloped together early this morning."
- Anthony complains Honora came asking about woods.

**Ch V "Jimmy's Affections"**
- Honora departs; Jimmy heartbroken briefly. Honora dinner farewell; kisses Moira in bed; "Why are you so afraid of me, Mr. Nannock?" Moira feigned sleep.
- Charlie Purdue kisses Moira in race; Jimmy jealous; fights Charlie in wood ("Say you're sorry"). Moira witnesses, goes to Paul. Jimmy's "conquering manhood."

**Ch VI "Mrs. Baffall's Dream"**
- Paul goes to London secretly; learns he has a fatal illness ("It's death, Mrs. Baffall"). Night walk; Mrs. Baffall dreams and comes out with candle; talk: "Good-night" not "good-bye."

**Ch VII "Over the Hills and Far Away"**
- Paul dreams of Moira's mother ("Moira!—my Moira!"), tries to write will: "To Moira, beloved of my heart now and always, I give——" dies at foot of stairs. Patience sits holding him, carries him to room, locks it.
- Moira reads only "beloved of my heart"; Patience's tears.
- Honora returns, takes children on day away; Matthew Shandler (man in black, cousin/"second cousin on his father's side") claims estate. Shandler sells everything. Alice goes to Baffalls. Jimmy to London via Baffall business post. Moira and Patience leave for London. Moira at grave: "Good-bye, Old Paul—for ever and ever." Jimmy and Moira farewell on hill in rain: "I shall see you again."

**BOOK II**
**Ch I "The Call of the World"**
- Patience (savings, retirement) and Moira in narrow street in Chelsea, top rooms (Locker Street). Moira bored, longing.
- Moira goes to Opera (Faust) with a common girl from downstairs; "Good Lord!" Girl says somebody else takes her out.
- Moira writes to Alice (who now "Alice Vickery", London, staying with Baffalls); Alice answers "DEAREST MOIRA". Moira visits Baffalls' grand house (gold and mirrors). Alice patronising ("the dear old things are so stuffy").
- Moira visits Jimmy at warehouse (Cheapside); told he's gone.

**Ch II "Jimmy—and a Matter of Food"**
- Jimmy at warehouse (Mr. Baffall recommended him), boarding-house near Camden Town (wheezy landlady). Fights weedy youth (shoe thrown). Writes; editor (flaxen hair, pipe, boy William) buys; Jimmy gets 16 shillings; later magazine closes ("we've doubled up"). Jimmy sacked; moves to rooms off Holborn; British Museum reading-room; tea shop.

**Ch III "The Complete Letter-Writer"**
- Patience writes boastful letter on black-edged paper to Baffalls. Baffall suspects bluff; Rev. Purdue receives; Baffall proposes Charlie lodge with Patience ("Patience Roe has rooms to spare").
- Anthony Ditchburn (now beggar, coffee-house, Fleet Street area) writes begging letter to Rev. Purdue; Purdue sends £1 and tells Charlie.
- Charlie arrives at Moira's room.

**Ch IV "The Man in Print"**
- Charlie studies medicine (failing); takes Moira to restaurant, then music hall; cab; "Locker Street" house. Charlie moves downstairs; Ditchburn pesters him (drinks, tobacco).
- Ditchburn finds Jimmy via British Museum; Jimmy's novel in print "By James Larrance"; Moira writes to Jimmy; reply: "My dear, dear Moira" from Jimmy.

**Ch V "Another Taste of Bohemia"**
- Moira visits Jimmy's rooms (Holborn court); landlady dispute; Moira cooks breakfast (rasher & eggs). Charlie & Ditchburn arrive; lunch; cheque £5 5s.

**Ch VI "Charlie Plunges"**
- Charlie's background (father's ultimatum; father gave £50 draft, last). Charlie tries painting, writing. Proposes to Moira ("Not alone, dear"). Moira: "I think so." Charlie kisses her.

**Ch VII "Dreams"**
- Jimmy's novel rejected; publisher (big-bearded) takes it at loss; Jimmy owes £6 5s 9d. Bennett Godsby (actor) wants play; Jimmy writes it; paid £20.
- Moira tells Jimmy she will marry Charlie. Jimmy: "I hope you'll be very happy."

**Ch VIII "The Sides of the 'Buses O!"**
- Play produced; Bennett Godsby's co-authorship; paragraphs garble credit; Mrs. Baffall, Alice, Baffall attend first night. Jimmy walks home, sees name on omnibus.

**Ch IX "The Dawn"**
- Night of play; Moira waits outside; Charlie visits; Moira comes to Charlie's room; Charlie seduces her (she is distressed). "I didn't know, Charlie."

**BOOK III**
**Ch I "'It'll Be All Right'"**
- Moira pregnant. Charlie tries borrowing from Patience. Charlie's father refuses him ("Get out of my house"). Charlie drinks, is knocked down by carriage/cab, dying; asks for Jimmy.

**Ch II "Jimmy Quixote"**
- Jimmy successful (cheque £100, Ashby Feak rival for Alice). Charlie dies; "I wronged her... she'll be all alone... It'll be all right... Tell her from me."
- Jimmy promises to marry Moira. Patience reports Moira gone.
- Rev. Purdue visits Jimmy. Jimmy tells Moira he will marry her; she accepts.

**Ch III "Two Ways of Love"**
- Jimmy marries Moira at church in rain. Estranged. Baby girl born (named Moira). Jimmy courts Alice; Ashby Feak returns; Jimmy claims secret. Moira visits Jimmy's rooms: "Is there someone else?" Jimmy: "Yes."

**Ch IV "The Long Night"**
- Anthony Ditchburn steals Moira's letters to Jimmy from box; shows Jimmy; Jimmy drinks heavily. Moira's letters reveal: child is Jimmy's, never loved Charlie.
- Jimmy goes to cottage, tries to kill Moira (throttles); she says "Yes—kill me"; he flees.
- Moira comes to Jimmy's rooms; sets him to work; "the long night."

**Ch V "If I Might Die!"**
- Jimmy reads letters. Moira refused to return; Patience says she'll come back; Jimmy takes baby.

**Ch VI "The Spirit of Old Paul"**
- Jimmy takes baby to Daisley Cross inn; Moira comes; Jimmy speaks of love; reunion at Old Paul's grave. "Love had shown them the way." THE END (Book 1).

## BOOK 2 OF 2: "Tinman" by Tom Gallon (Gutenberg 48989; Small, Maynard & Co., Boston, 1907)
Contents: Part I ch I–VI; Part II ch I–XIII.

### PART I
**Ch I "What I Found in the Wood"** (narrator: Charles Avaline, writing from old age in prison/garret)
- Narrator is ward of **Jervis Fanshawe** (manager of Patton & Co., Bloomsbury house, office in City). Fanshawe: ~35, bald-ish, long clean-shaven face, thin nose, deep cut in chin, paper-knife.
- **Gavin Hockley**: big young man, moustache, swagger, cane; at Fanshawe's dinner; Fanshawe fears him. Hockley: "Hammerstone Market" for fishing.
- Dream: Hockley's face, weapon in narrator's hand, Hockley dead at feet.
- Hammerstone Market: narrator stays at the *George*. Meets **Barbara Patton** in wood (singing, 18; daughter of **Mr. Patton**). Patton's house outside town. Hockley lounging, tramps narrator's canvas.
- Fanshawe seen at pool.

**Ch II "And What I Lost"**
- Fanshawe says he wants to marry Barbara; narrator says she loves him. Fanshawe's face convulsed with rage.
- Dinner at Patton's: doctor's story about a man who set two men against each other (parable of guilt); **Lucas Savell** (good-humoured cousin) engaged to Barbara; toast. Narrator's glass snaps.
- Garden: Barbara's whispered "I promised a year ago"; Hockley grabs her; narrator strikes Hockley (goes down steps). Fanshawe praises. Hockley threatens narrator, "strike him dead."

**Ch III "Her Wedding Day"**
- Fanshawe admits he "wanted her," she laughed. Hockley wants money; Fanshawe in his power; cards game at Fanshawe's rooms, narrator loses ~£30 (I.O.U.). Hockley's jibe "Lucky at cards, unlucky in love."
- Barbara's wedding (to Lucas Savell). Barbara's note: "my poor Prince Charlie"; "dream-love always"; signed BARBARA.
- Supper with Hockley and Fanshawe at *George*; Hockley's "pretty bride" toast.

**Ch IV "The Killing of the Lie"**
- Quarrel: Hockley says Barbara "a lady of many loves"; narrator attacks him; Fanshawe claims narrator tried to murder. Next morning Hockley gone. Narrator goes to Hockley's rooms in Lincoln's Inn Fields; kills him with sword ("I've killed Gavin Hockley—and his lie").

**Ch V "Alas! For Poor Prince Charlie!"**
- Fanshawe confesses: he arranged it; had been in Hockley's clutches; forged; wanted Barbara. Narrator says he'll not contradict. Narrator arrested in Holborn room; gives woman his last money. Trial: "Guilty"; judge's sentence; death. Fanshawe testifies against.

**Ch VI "I Leave the World"**
- Condemned; dreams of Barbara in wood; she comes (in black), says "I will reach you—God willing—before they kill you." Narrator tells her "a child you love... a friend who will strike." Barbara promises silence. Reprieved: penal servitude for life, "On account of my youth."

### PART II
**Ch I "Mine Enemy"** (prison No. 145, 20 years; tinsmith)
- Released after 20 years (aged ~40); governor; old, grey. Outside gate: Fanshawe (thin, black-bearded short beard, grey roots). "Tinman" name later. Fanshawe takes money; flees to London with narrator; says "Barbara... shall see her again."

**Ch II "Ghosts"**
- Fanshawe lodging in riverside street; girl **Moggs** (~15, scruffy, cockney). Fanshawe reveals plan; **Murray Olivant** (heavy, dark hair, cold voice, well-dressed, rich) employs them.
- Narrator goes to Hammerstone Market in winter; sees young Barbara Savell (daughter of Barbara) with **Arnold Millard** (Olivant's half-brother, painter) in wood; sees house; hears her sing; "Barbara, you have your mother's voice." Barbara Savell is Barbara's child (the elder Barbara's child). Narrator told the elder Barbara dead (died at sea).

**Ch III "I Enter Upon Servitude"**
- Named "Tinman" by Olivant. Fanshawe reveals Olivant wants young Barbara; Lucas Savell broke, ruined; Olivant owns business. Narrator sent to Hammerstone Market as Olivant's servant. Lucas Savell in mourning; Barbara Savell ("Have you ever seen ghosts, Tinman?"). Face staring through window (elder Barbara).

**Ch IV "The Coming of the Wolves"**
- Barbara Savell and Tinman; narrator reveals friendship. Arnold Millard; Olivant insults Barbara at dinner (Dawkins, smiling man, present). Arnold's knife; Olivant stays; Barbara flees. Olivant grabs Barbara on stairs. Narrator blocks him: "I killed a man once."

**Ch V "I Touch Disaster"**
- Narrator sleeps across Barbara's doorway; Olivant threatens; Olivant plans to leave for London. Narrator tells Arnold to meet Barbara at wood path at eight; Fanshawe overheard. Olivant & Dawkins capture narrator in Olivant's room, tie with towel, gag, take note.

**Ch VI "Love With the Veiled Face"**
- Dawkins takes forged note to lure Barbara to London. Narrator frees himself with towel, climbs out window; elder Barbara (veiled) seen at terrace; Lucas Savell's window. Olivant says Barbara ran away with Arnold. Arnold broken; "I'll kill him." Fanshawe: "The dead come alive... Barbara."
- Elder Barbara speaks: "I've come back—my dear—to save my child."

**Ch VII "News of the Prisoner"**
- Elder Barbara's story: husband Lucas Savell; she faked death on voyage; stewardess helped; name Barbara Avaline; lives at cottage, needlework. Plans: narrator to London to meet her at Trafalgar Square.
- In London: Olivant's cab; narrator warns Olivant; Olivant gets a letter from Dawkins demanding £500 for Barbara's address. Moggs at Fanshawe's house: Dawkins is waiting.

**Ch VIII "I Assist the Enemy"**
- Narrator confronts Dawkins; Dawkins refuses. Fanshawe returns; confesses fear of ghost of Barbara. Moggs's plan: Barbara Savell found at Moggs' room (Board School friend). Fanshawe overhears. Olivant and Dawkins come; Olivant's rooms; Arnold bursts in, Olivant denies she's there.

**Ch IX "I Know the Way at Last"**
- Policeman removes Arnold. Olivant plans fake voyage on *Eaglet* (steamer), hiding in Lincoln's Inn Fields rooms. Narrator secures rooms with duplicate key. Narrator kneels to Olivant in Holborn; elder Barbara finds young Barbara asleep at her lodging. Narrator resolves to kill Olivant.

**Ch X "Too Late!"**
- Narrator buys sailor's knife in marine-store shop; Fanshawe prompts "a knife" to Narrator. Narrator goes to Lincoln's Inn Fields, finds Olivant dead with knife in breast; someone (Arnold) had struck first.
- Narrator sends elder Barbara to take daughter home. Fanshawe overhears; tells narrator he'd kill...

**Ch XI "I Tell the Truth"**
- Narrator finds Fanshawe waiting at door (he killed Olivant with knife bought earlier; keys). Fanshawe takes tickets; Dawkins arrives; Narrator says Olivant sailed. Next morning Fanshawe sails on *Eaglet* with the tickets, which narrator had lost.
- Arnold meets narrator at station; lies about Olivant. Narrator tells elder Barbara he killed Olivant (lie to save Arnold). She goes back to Lucas Savell.

**Ch XII "The Haunted Man"**
- Lucas Savell sees Barbara Savell reunited with elder Barbara; Lucas suffers stroke; never speaks again. Narrator learns Fanshawe killed Olivant (confession in room; keys). *Eaglet* wrecked off Ushant; Fanshawe lost; newspaper: "Mr. Murray Olivant" lost in wreck (dead man was Olivant, buried as unknown).

**Ch XIII "I Face the World Again"**
- Narrator in hospital, released; wedding of Barbara Savell and Arnold Millard at Hammerstone Market church; Barbara kisses narrator. Narrator reunited with elder Barbara in wood; "Charlie, I took your name once... let me take it now." Narrator is Charles Avaline; the narrative ends with "THE END."

## Key names summary
- Book 1: Paul Nannock ("Old Paul"), Moira, Jimmy (James Larrance; "Jimmy Quixote"), Alice (Vickery), Patience (Roe), Anthony Ditchburn, Rev. Temple Purdue, Charlie Purdue, Daniel & Mrs. Flora Baffall, Honora Jackman, Matthew Shandler, Ashby Feak, Bennett Godsby, Mrs. Bennett Godsby, Murray? (no), Arnold? (no), Lucas? (no).
- Book 2: Charles Avaline (narrator, "Tinman", "No. 145"), Jervis Fanshawe, Gavin Hockley, Barbara Patton (later Savell; elder Barbara, "Barbara Avaline"), Mr. Patton, Lucas Savell, Barbara Savell (daughter), Arnold Millard, Murray Olivant, Dawkins, Moggs, Lucas, Patton, Henry Howard (sailor survivor).
